fullDescription: ❄ BRG Arctic Horizon ☀ Cool blue skies. Drifting white mist. Clean aqua water. A world that feels calm, cold and cinematic, without a heavy shader. ❄ Welcome to Arctic Horizon BRGamers Arctic Horizon is a lightweight, Arctic-inspired atmosphere pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition . It keeps the classic blocky look you already love, then wraps your world in a cooler, mistier and more atmospheric mood. Distant mountains fade softly into a pale cyan haze, forests sit under drifting white mist, lakes turn a clean aqua blue, and the sky and moon get a fresh, polished look. Everything in this pack was made from scratch by BRGamers. It does not copy any other creator's files, textures or code. The pack is only about 250 KB , so it installs in seconds and is gentle on phones and tablets. ✦ Why You Will Like It Lightweight: a tiny download, no shader loader and no heavy effects. Vanilla-friendly: block textures are untouched, so your builds still look like Minecraft. Atmospheric: layered fog, mist and cool tints give the whole world a calm mood. Easy to install: open the file, activate it and play. Customizable: one number in a text file makes the fog lighter or thicker. 🌫 Layered Fog and Mist Fog is the heart of this pack. Instead of one flat fog for every biome, Arctic Horizon uses seven different fog styles , each tuned for the kind of place you are standing in. Fog starts far enough away that the terrain around you stays clear, then slowly thickens with distance so faraway hills and mountains melt into the horizon. White Mist: forests, birch forests, taiga, swamps, jungles, meadows and rivers get the thickest, softest mist. It starts close, so trees fade into a gentle white veil. Snow Haze: snowy plains, frozen rivers, groves and mountain peaks use a bright, pale-blue haze that feels crisp and cold. Open Sky Fog: plains, savannas and hills get a clean blue-white distance fade that keeps the view wide and open. Warm Haze: deserts and badlands use a slightly warmer pale haze, so they do not look unnaturally icy. Ocean Fog: oceans get a cool blue distance fade, and deep oceans use a darker, deeper tone with a longer view. Cave Fog: dripstone caves, lush caves and the deep dark get a cool, dark blue fog for a moody feeling underground. 🌊 Aqua Water Water uses a clean aqua-blue surface color with a slightly more transparent look, so lakes and rivers feel fresh instead of flat. Shallow biomes lean light and turquoise, while deep oceans use a darker, deeper blue. Underwater fog colors are tuned to match, so diving feels calm and consistent with the rest of the world. ☁ Soft Custom Clouds The clouds were redrawn as soft, tileable shapes with a faint cool tint. They sit nicely against the blue sky and fit the Arctic mood without looking harsh or noisy. ☀ Redrawn Sun with Light Rays The sun has a warm white-gold glow with thin rays of light spreading out from it. The rays pointing downward are the longest and brightest, so the sun looks like it is shining down over the land. Look toward the sun at sunrise or sunset to enjoy it. 🌙 Moon with 8 Phases The moon has a cool blue-white tone, soft crater detail and all eight phases. Nights keep a calm, moonlit feeling, and the moon looks great against the deep blue night sky. 🌿 Cool Natural Foliage Tints Grass, foliage, spruce and birch colormaps lean slightly cooler and fresher, so green areas match the blue sky and mist. The result is natural and balanced, with no neon colors. Cold biomes feel colder, and warm biomes stay green and healthy. ⚡ Performance Arctic Horizon is a normal resource pack, so it does not need a shader loader or any special render pass. The download is tiny, and it keeps all the vanilla block textures, so it is a good choice for Android phones, tablets and older devices. Results depend on your device, so there are no FPS promises here, but because nothing heavy is added, the pack is designed to stay light. 📦 Compatibility Edition: Minecraft Bedrock Edition (Android, iOS, Windows) Version: 1.21 and newer Vibrant Visuals: not required. Keep it off for the intended look. Shader loader: not required. Other packs: if another pack changes fog, sky or clouds, move Arctic Horizon above it in the list. 🛠 How to Install Download the .mcpack file. Open the file. Minecraft will import it automatically. Go to Settings → Global Resources . Activate BRGamers Arctic Horizon and move it to the top. Create or open a world and enjoy. Updating? Remove the old version first so the game does not load the cached one. 🎛 Customize It Want less fog? Open the fogs folder inside the pack and find the fog file for the biome you want to change. Each file has a value called fog_start . Raise it (for example from 0.20 to 0.40) and the fog starts farther away, which gives you a clearer view. Lower it for thicker mist. If you want to change the sky or water color, edit the colors in biomes_client.json . ⚠ What This Pack Is Not To keep things honest, here is exactly what to expect. Arctic Horizon is a standard resource pack , not a shader. That means it does not add real-time shadows, water reflections, wind-animated leaves, bloom or true volumetric god rays that pass through trees. The sun rays are part of the sun texture, so they are visible when you look at the sun. Fog and sky colors also stay the same through the day and night cycle. If you want those effects, they need a shader or Vibrant Visuals, and this pack does not claim to replace them. What it does give you is a clean, light and consistent Arctic atmosphere that works for everyone. ❓ FAQ Is this a shader? No. It is a lightweight atmosphere resource pack. Does it need Vibrant Visuals? No. Keep Vibrant Visuals off. Will it lag my phone? It is very small and adds no heavy effects, so it should be gentle on most devices. Nothing changed after installing. What do I do? Check that the pack is active in Global Resources, move it to the top, remove any older copy and disable other packs that change fog or sky. Can I use it in a video or modpack? Yes, please credit BRGamers and link back to this page. 💙 Credits and Support Created by BRGamers . All assets are original. If you enjoy the pack, leave a rating, share a screenshot and tell your friends. Feedback helps the pack get better with every update. Stay cool. Stay misty. Enjoy the horizon. ☀

title: SERPENT VISUALS
description: SERPENT VISUALS brings a vivid, glowing Vibrant Visuals atmosphere to Minecraft Bedrock — cozy campfire-lit nights, golden sunsets, lush vivid lakes, misty rain, a fiery nether, and glowing gold-lit caves.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: SERPENT VISUALS is an original Vibrant Visuals atmosphere pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, built to turn ordinary daylight and night cycles into something vivid, warm and glowing. It doesn't touch any block models or vanilla textures — it rewrites how light, sky, fog and color behave, using Minecraft's own Vibrant Visuals (deferred lighting) system. COZY, WARM NIGHTS Villages at night feel inviting rather than flat. Campfires, torches and lanterns glow a richer warm orange, casting a visible pool of light on the grass and nearby walls. The night sky is a deep, soft navy rather than plain black, with gentle drifting clouds and a calm, moody atmosphere perfect for a quiet evening around a fire. VIVID LAKES AND FORESTS Daytime water is clean, saturated and blue, with soft reflections of the sky and trees. Forest greens are rich and alive rather than dull, so a lakeside view full of trees feels lush and vibrant under a bright, clear sky. GOLDEN, CINEMATIC SUNSETS Sunrise and sunset get real presence: a bigger, brighter glowing sun sits low on the horizon, with the sky sweeping from warm gold near the sun into soft lavender and dusky blue higher up. Treelines turn into dramatic silhouettes against the glow, and a light haze near the ground adds depth to the scene. SOFT, OVERCAST RAIN Rainy weather shifts the whole mood — flatter, cooler grey-green light, a denser low haze, and muted colors that feel properly overcast, so wet village streets and rainy days actually look and feel different from a clear day. A FIERY NETHER The Nether leans harder into its heat: a deeper red-orange haze, brighter glowing lava, and warmer embers from fire and magma blocks, so lava oceans and basalt cliffs feel properly dangerous and alive. GLOWING GOLDEN CAVES Lush Caves and Dripstone Caves carry their own warm gold-amber glow, so hanging vines and glow lichen light up the stone around them instead of sitting in flat grey light — caves feel like a place worth exploring, not just a hole in the ground. RICHER COLOR GRADING THROUGHOUT On top of every scene above, SERPENT VISUALS applies its own color grading — boosted saturation across highlights, midtones and shadows, a touch more contrast, and a slightly raised exposure — so colors stay vivid and alive everywhere, without tipping into neon or unnatural territory. WHAT THIS PACK DOES NOT DO To keep expectations honest: SERPENT VISUALS works entirely through Minecraft's documented Vibrant Visuals resource-pack system — sky, fog, lighting, color grading and water. It cannot add camera depth-of-field blur, bloom halos beyond normal emissive glow, film grain, or any cinematic camera effect, and it cannot change tree types or block placement. Those need a different kind of mod entirely. What changes here is color, light and atmosphere. REQUIREMENTS Minimum engine version 1.21.100. Vibrant Visuals must be turned on in both Video settings and your world's settings — without that toggle enabled, none of this pack's sky, lighting or fog changes will appear. SERPENT VISUALS is built entirely from original, self-authored settings — no files, textures or code from any other shader or resource pack are used. Enjoy the glow! Credits SERPENT VISUALS : created and tuned entirely by yogamerzyt Minecraft : Mojang Studios / Microsoft. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Mojang or Microsoft.

title: CELEB VISUALS
description: Celeb VISUALS is a biome-aware Vibrant Visuals shader. Jungles glow in teal haze with yellow-green sunrises, oceans sink into deep blue fog, nights turn teal and starry, and every biome gets its own light colour.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: Celeb VISUALS is a Vibrant Visuals shader for Minecraft Bedrock built around one idea: every biome should have its own light. Instead of giving the whole world one colour mood, it tints the sun, sky, ambient light, fog and water separately for each biome. Jungles get a blue-cyan daytime sky, teal-green haze that settles between the trees and teal water. At sunrise and sunset the horizon turns yellow-green, so the sun looks like it is shining through a humid canopy. Shadows lean teal instead of plain grey. Oceans and rivers sit under a deep blue sky and a dense blue fog that begins close to the player, so far shores dissolve into mist. The water surface is a deeper blue. Warm sunsets stay orange over the sea. Nights are teal. The sky shifts to deep navy at the top and teal towards the horizon, and the colour changes by biome: teal in default biomes and jungles, plum in cherry groves, icy blue in snowy biomes and ghostly violet in the pale garden. Rain keeps a soft grey fog, so wet days feel flat and muted instead of colourful. Cherry groves use rose-pink light and sky. The Nether burns ember red-orange. The End stays violet-magenta. Snowy biomes are icy blue, swamps murky olive, mushroom islands violet-pink, deserts and savannas amber, lush caves emerald and the deep dark eerie teal. Across all 88 biomes the pack uses 13 colour groups, and every biome points to its own light, sky and fog settings. Water is tinted to match each palette. Colour grading is richer than vanilla, with boosted saturation and ACES filmic tone mapping. Shadow maps are doubled in resolution so edges stay crisp. Compatibility. The pack contains no textures, so it works with any texture pack. It targets Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.100 or newer and uses only settings formats from 1.21.90 and below. Setup. Turn on Vibrant Visuals in Video settings. Place the pack at the top of your resource pack list. Do not stack it with other shaders. Remove older versions before importing. Limits. Aurora lights, shooting stars and glass-like clouds are not part of this pack, because Bedrock resource packs cannot create them. Creator & Credits

title: YG SHADER
description: YG SHADER brings a vivid, glowing Vibrant Visuals atmosphere to Minecraft Bedrock — pink sun rays in cherry blossom groves, green rays in forests, dramatic purple-violet sunsets, and a glowing violet mood in caves.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: YG SHADER is an original Vibrant Visuals atmosphere pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, built from the ground up to turn ordinary daylight and night cycles into something vivid, glowing and a little dreamlike. It doesn't touch any block models or vanilla textures — instead it rewrites how light, sky and fog behave, using Minecraft's own Vibrant Visuals (deferred lighting) system. COLOR-CODED SUN RAYS BY BIOME Every biome now has its own light-shaft color. Walk into a cherry blossom grove and the sunlight filtering through the petals glows a soft, dreamy pink. Step into a forest and the same light turns a rich, leafy green as it filters through the canopy. Jungles carry a deep humid green haze, deserts a warm dusty gold, swamps a murky olive-green, and snowy biomes a pale icy blue. Each mood is tuned individually through the biome's own fog settings, so the light always feels like it belongs to the place you're standing in. DRAMATIC, PURPLE-TINTED SKIES Sunrise and sunset no longer fade through plain orange. The sky now sweeps from warm gold into rose-pink and then deep violet-magenta before settling into night, giving every dawn and dusk a cinematic, almost aurora-like quality. Midday skies are a clean, saturated blue, and nights shift into a deep indigo-violet rather than flat black, with a cooler, slightly purple moonlight. STRONGER GLOW EVERYWHERE Light sources are noticeably brighter and more saturated: torches, lanterns, campfires, glowstone, sea lanterns, beacons, amethyst clusters, end rods and portals all glow harder and spill more color onto nearby blocks. Caves get their own atmosphere too — Lush Caves and Dripstone Caves now carry a glowing violet-purple haze, giving underground exploration a mysterious, otherworldly feel instead of flat grey stone lighting. RICHER COLOR GRADING On top of the sky and lighting changes, YG SHADER applies its own color grading pass — boosted saturation across highlights, midtones and shadows, a touch more contrast, and a slightly raised exposure — so colors read as vivid and alive rather than washed out, without ever tipping into neon or unnatural territory. WHAT THIS PACK DOES NOT DO To set expectations correctly: YG SHADER works entirely through Minecraft's documented Vibrant Visuals resource-pack system (sky, fog, lighting, color grading, water). It cannot create custom cloud shapes, floating glowing objects, or any effect that isn't part of that system — those would need a completely different kind of mod. What it changes is color, light and atmosphere, not geometry. REQUIREMENTS YG SHADER requires a Minecraft Bedrock version with Vibrant Visuals support, with Vibrant Visuals turned on in both Video settings and your world's settings. Without that toggle enabled, none of the pack's sky, lighting or fog changes will appear, so please double-check it's on if things don't look different after importing. YG SHADER is built entirely from original, self-authored settings and artwork — no files, textures or code from any other shader or resource pack are used. Enjoy the glow! Credits YG SHADER : created and tuned entirely by yogamerzyt Minecraft : Mojang Studios / Microsoft. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Mojang or Microsoft.

title: BASE VISUALS
description: BASE VISUALS is a lighting and atmosphere pack for Vibrant Visuals. It adds biome-coloured sun rays, golden-lavender sunsets, moonlit nights, glowing lanterns, water caustics and a vivid Nether and End. By Baku_Studio.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: BASE VISUALS: A Beautiful Base for Your Minecraft World BASE VISUALS is a lighting and atmosphere pack for Minecraft Bedrock, built for Vibrant Visuals. It keeps the blocks, textures and feel of classic Minecraft and changes only the light around them. Instead of one grey-white light for the whole world, every biome gets its own colour of sunlight, haze, sky and water. Step into a cherry grove and the rays turn soft pink. Walk into a jungle and the light becomes deep emerald. Every place feels different. What You Get Biome-coloured sun rays. The pack tints the volumetric fog that carries the light shafts, so the rays take the colour of the biome around you. It covers all 89 biomes with 39 hand-tuned light themes, including caves, oceans and the other dimensions. A few examples: Cherry Grove: rose-pink rays with a dreamy glow Jungle and Bamboo Jungle: emerald and lime-green shafts Birch and Forest: warm champagne-gold light Dark Forest: golden light cutting through dark canopies Autumn Forest: fiery orange rays over vivid red and orange leaves Taiga: cool mint-teal light Snowy Biomes: icy blue rays Desert, Savanna and Badlands: amber, orange and terracotta light Oceans: aqua, turquoise and deep blue Mushroom Fields: violet-magenta haze Golden-lavender sunsets and sunrises. At dusk and dawn the sky blends from soft lavender at the top to peach and rose near the horizon. The sunlight turns golden-orange, then deepens toward pink as the sun sinks. Rays streaming through trees at this hour are the pack's signature look. Moonlit nights. Night skies are a deep indigo-violet with soft purple-white moonlight and a bright glow around the moon. Warm, coloured local lights. Torches, lanterns, campfires, candles, glowstone, lava and other light sources cast their own coloured light on nearby blocks. Soul torches glow blue, copper torches glow green, and amethyst glows violet. Lantern-lit paths at night are one of the pack's best moments. Water with caustics. Shallow water shows animated, net-like caustic patterns on the floor, and water is tuned to look clean and turquoise, with a subtle tint from each biome. The caustics texture was created from scratch for this pack. Moody rain. During rain the haze turns a cool blue-grey, only lightly tinted by the biome, so storms feel wet and atmospheric. A vivid End. The End has a deep violet sky, a magenta glow near the horizon and a soft lavender beam of light, with its own colour grading. A redesigned Nether. fullDescription: ABHU VISUALS is a Vibrant Visuals pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition that gives every biome its own colour of light. Walk into a cherry grove at sunrise and the beams drifting through the blossoms glow soft pink. Step into a forest and the same sunlight turns fresh emerald. Cross into a snowy taiga and the rays cool to a silvery blue, while deserts and savannas burn with warm amber. The pack never replaces your textures or changes gameplay. It simply repaints the atmosphere, so your world feels like a different place wherever you travel. The look is built on three ideas. First, directional lighting: the sun and moon each carry a biome-specific tint, and that tint reaches blocks, leaves, water surfaces and the sky. Second, volumetric fog: every featured biome has a thin, coloured haze that catches the light and turns it into visible shafts between trunks, hills and clouds. Third, a gentle day and night cycle: sunrise and sunset blend each tint toward a warm glow, and nights switch to a cool moonlit palette that matches the biome you are standing in. Featured biomes include Cherry Grove, Forest, Flower Forest, Birch Forest, Plains, Sunflower Plains, Taiga, Old Growth Taiga, Snowy Taiga, Snowy Plains, Windswept Hills, Jungle, Bamboo Jungle, Savanna and Desert. Every other biome keeps its normal Mojang look, but its sunlight is still gently re-tinted so swamps, mushroom fields, pale gardens, ice spikes, badlands and the like feel consistent with the rest of the pack. Everything in ABHU VISUALS is original. The pack contains no copied shaders, textures or code. It is made entirely from the official Vibrant Visuals data files that Minecraft already supports, namely lighting, fog and client biome definitions, and all colour values were chosen by hand for this project. Light intensity follows the current vanilla scale, so exposure, shadows and the day cycle stay balanced and nothing looks blown out. Because it relies on official data files, no mods, launchers, OptiFine or Iris are needed. It works in the standard Bedrock app on any device that supports Vibrant Visuals. Performance depends on your hardware, but the pack adds no extra textures and only a few small configuration files, so it asks for very little beyond what Vibrant Visuals already uses. How to install: open the downloaded file with Minecraft so it imports automatically, go to Settings, then Global Resources, and activate ABHU VISUALS. Next open Settings, then Video, and switch Vibrant Visuals on. Load a world, and for the best first impression travel to a cherry grove or a forest around sunrise or sunset, when light shafts are strongest. Compatibility: designed for Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.100 and newer, including the 26.x releases. Older versions do not support the Vibrant Visuals pack format, and Vibrant Visuals itself must be enabled or you will see no difference. The Nether and the End are intentionally left untouched so their carefully tuned vanilla atmospheres are preserved. Two strengths are included. The standard edition aims for a natural, balanced look, while the Strong edition pushes colour, haze and beam density for a more dramatic, screenshot-style result. A small Test pack is also provided so you can confirm that your device loads Vibrant Visuals packs correctly before judging the look. Credits: created and designed by GURJAR. Minecraft and Vibrant Visuals belong to Mojang Studios and Microsoft. This pack is an independent fan-made creation and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Mojang or Microsoft. Feel free to share it, but please keep the credit to GURJAR when you do. Feature list Biome-specific sun and moon colours with a warm blend at sunrise and sunset Coloured volumetric haze that turns sunlight into visible light shafts 15 featured biomes with their own palette, remaining Overworld biomes gently re-tinted Light intensity on the current vanilla scale, so exposure and shadows stay balanced Nether and End left untouched Three files: Standard, Strong (more colour and haze) and a Test pack for checking that packs load 100% original configuration, no copied shaders, textures or code No mods, launchers, OptiFine or Iris required Installation Open the downloaded .mcpack file with Minecraft so it imports itself. Settings > Global Resources > activate ABHU VISUALS (it must appear under Active). Settings > Video > turn Vibrant Visuals on. Load a world and look toward the sun in a cherry grove or forest at sunrise or sunset. If you copy the files by hand, the pack folder must contain manifest.json directly inside it (not inside another folder). Requirements and compatibility Minecraft Bedrock Edition 1.21.100 or newer, including the 26.x versions A device that supports Vibrant Visuals Not for Java Edition Known limitations Vibrant Visuals must be enabled, otherwise the pack has no visible effect. This pack uses Minecraft's official data files, so it cannot match the look of third-party shader packs; it recolours the light and haze Vibrant Visuals already renders. The strongest beams appear near sunrise and sunset and through trees or hills; rain and thunderstorms mute them. The pack replaces the client definition of its 19 featured biome IDs. Those biomes keep default grass and foliage tint and default biome music. If anything looks off, try the Standard edition and note which biome. Results may need small colour tuning per device and version. Credits and legal Created and designed by GURJAR. Minecraft and Vibrant Visuals are trademarks of Mojang Studios and Microsoft. They are listed in this order, and the last one is selected automatically, so most players never need to open the dropdown at all. Water only. All, Nether keeps fog. All except lava. All. This is the recommended one and the default. What changes Water. Vanilla fog ends at 60 blocks. Removed, so you can see across the sea floor. Lava. Vanilla fog ends at 0.64 blocks. Choose "All, Nether keeps fog" if you want to keep that closed-in atmosphere. Vibrant Visuals Tested with Vibrant Visuals enabled. Water, lava and the Nether are cleared exactly the same as without it. One thing this pack cannot touch: Vibrant Visuals has its own volumetric fog, the hazy light shafts around light sources. That is a separate system from biome fog, so no resource pack can change it. It has its own toggle in the video settings if you don't want it. Vibrant Visuals also uses its own render distance slider, so how far you can see is capped by that rather than by this pack. About the comparison screenshots Vanilla water fog is not constant. Right after you dive it sits at about 15 blocks, then it opens up over roughly 30 seconds and settles at 60. The before shots on this page were taken after it had fully settled. That is the fairest comparison, not the murkiest possible frame. Important: put this pack at the top of your active list This pack replaces the biome fog definitions, and only the topmost pack that does so is used. If another pack sits above this one, this one does nothing. Notes Resource pack only. No behaviour pack, no scripts, no commands. Achievements are unaffected. Fog is not render distance. You still only see as far as your render distance setting allows. On a server, that server's render distance still applies. Servers that use the /fog command will override this pack, because the command layer takes priority. Removing weather fog is a real visibility advantage in PvP. Check your server or tournament rules. This is not an X-ray. Block rendering is untouched, so hidden blocks stay hidden. Lava looks completely normal from the outside and only turns clear once the camera is inside it. Per-biome water colours are preserved. All 94 vanilla biome entries are kept as they are and only the fog reference is changed, so swamp water is still swamp water. All four levels work the same on every device, including phones and tablets. The pack name and description are translated into all 29 languages Minecraft offers, so it shows in your own language in game. 67 files, 31 KB. No textures, just fog definitions. Installation Download the .mcpack and open it. Enable it under Global Resources in settings. Move it to the top of the list and pick a level from the dropdown. Development notes Four things that took the longest to get right, in case they help other pack makers. Your own namespace. Fog definitions in the minecraft: namespace cannot be overridden from a resource pack. A file that reuses a vanilla fog identifier is simply ignored. This pack defines its own fog, kentotukun:no_fog, points every biome's fog_identifier at it, and sets remove_all_prior_fog to true. Two biome formats. Biomes are now defined in two places: the older biomes_client.json and newer per-biome files in the biomes folder. Some biomes, including the deep dark, lush caves, the pale garden and every mutated variant, exist only in the newer format. Replacing only the older file leaves fog in those biomes. fog_start. Fog density is calculated between fog_start and fog_end. A fog_start of 0 leaves a faint tint at every distance. Moving fog_start beyond the visible range is what removes fog completely. memory_tier. Subpacks with different memory tiers are picked by device memory, so a low-memory phone may not get the level you meant as the default. Giving every subpack the same tier makes the game pick the last one in the list on every device. fullDescription: AAUKA VISUALS is a Vibrant Visuals pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition that gives every biome its own colour of light. Walk into a cherry grove at sunrise and the beams drifting through the blossoms glow soft pink. Step into a forest and the same sunlight turns fresh emerald. Cross into a snowy taiga and the rays cool to a silvery blue, while deserts and savannas burn with warm amber. The pack never replaces your textures or changes gameplay. It simply repaints the atmosphere, so your world feels like a different place wherever you travel. The look is built on three ideas. First, directional lighting: the sun and moon each carry a biome-specific tint, and that tint reaches blocks, leaves, water surfaces and the sky. Second, volumetric fog: every featured biome has a thin, coloured haze that catches the light and turns it into visible shafts between trunks, hills and clouds. Third, a gentle day and night cycle: sunrise and sunset blend each tint toward a warm glow, and nights switch to a cool moonlit palette that matches the biome you are standing in. Featured biomes include Cherry Grove, Forest, Flower Forest, Birch Forest, Plains, Sunflower Plains, Taiga, Old Growth Taiga, Snowy Taiga, Snowy Plains, Windswept Hills, Jungle, Bamboo Jungle, Savanna and Desert. Every other biome keeps its normal Mojang look, but its sunlight is still gently re-tinted so swamps, mushroom fields, pale gardens, ice spikes, badlands and the like feel consistent with the rest of the pack. Everything in AAUKA VISUALS is original. The pack contains no copied shaders, textures or code. It is made entirely from the official Vibrant Visuals data files that Minecraft already supports, namely lighting, fog and client biome definitions, and all colour values were chosen by hand for this project. Light intensity follows the current vanilla scale, so exposure, shadows and the day cycle stay balanced and nothing looks blown out. Because it relies on official data files, no mods, launchers, OptiFine or Iris are needed. It works in the standard Bedrock app on any device that supports Vibrant Visuals. Performance depends on your hardware, but the pack adds no extra textures and only a few small configuration files, so it asks for very little beyond what Vibrant Visuals already uses. How to install: open the downloaded file with Minecraft so it imports automatically, go to Settings, then Global Resources, and activate AAUKA VISUALS. Next open Settings, then Video, and switch Vibrant Visuals on. Load a world, and for the best first impression travel to a cherry grove or a forest around sunrise or sunset, when light shafts are strongest. Compatibility: designed for Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.120 and newer, including the 26.x releases. Older versions do not support the Vibrant Visuals pack format, and Vibrant Visuals itself must be enabled or you will see no difference. The Nether and the End are intentionally left untouched so their carefully tuned vanilla atmospheres are preserved. A Safe edition is included for anyone who wants the lowest possible risk. It only re-tints sunlight and moonlight and does not touch any biome definitions, so grass, water, music and sounds are guaranteed to stay exactly as Mojang made them. The full edition adds coloured volumetric haze for the featured biomes and is the one that produces the strongest, most colourful beams. Credits: created and designed by GURJAR. Minecraft and Vibrant Visuals belong to Mojang Studios and Microsoft. This pack is an independent fan-made creation and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Mojang or Microsoft. Feel free to share it, but please keep the credit to GURJAR when you do. Feature list Biome-specific sun and moon colours with a warm blend at sunrise and sunset Coloured volumetric haze that turns sunlight into visible light shafts 15 featured biomes with their own palette, remaining Overworld biomes gently re-tinted Light intensity on the current vanilla scale, so exposure and shadows stay balanced Nether and End left untouched Two editions: Full (coloured haze) and Safe (tinted light only) 100% original configuration, no copied shaders, textures or code No mods, launchers, OptiFine or Iris required Installation Open the downloaded .mcpack file with Minecraft so it imports itself. Settings > Global Resources > activate AAUKA VISUALS. Settings > Video > turn Vibrant Visuals on. Load a world and look toward the sun in a cherry grove or forest at sunrise or sunset. If you copy the files by hand, the pack folder must contain manifest.json directly inside it (not inside another folder). Requirements and compatibility Minecraft Bedrock Edition 1.21.120 or newer, including the 26.x versions A device that supports Vibrant Visuals Not for Java Edition Known limitations Vibrant Visuals must be enabled, otherwise the pack has no visible effect. The strongest beams appear near sunrise and sunset and through trees or hills; rain and thunderstorms mute them. The Full edition replaces the client definition of its 19 featured biome IDs. Those biomes keep default grass and foliage tint and default biome music. If anything looks off, use the Safe edition. Results may need small colour tuning per device and version. fullDescription: CLASSIC VISUALS: Classic Minecraft, Beautiful Light CLASSIC VISUALS is a lighting and atmosphere pack for Minecraft Bedrock, built for Vibrant Visuals. It keeps the blocks, textures and feel of classic Minecraft and changes only the light around them. Instead of one grey-white light for the whole world, every biome gets its own colour of sunlight, haze, sky and water. Step into a cherry grove and the rays turn soft pink. Walk into a jungle and the light becomes deep emerald. Every biome feels like a different place. What You Get Biome-coloured sun rays. The pack tints the volumetric fog that carries the light shafts, so the rays take the colour of the biome around you. It covers all 89 biomes with 39 hand-tuned light themes, including caves, oceans and the other dimensions. A few examples: Cherry Grove: rose-pink rays with a dreamy glow Jungle and Bamboo Jungle: emerald and lime-green shafts Birch and Forest: warm champagne-gold light Dark Forest: golden light cutting through dark canopies Autumn Forest: fiery orange rays Taiga: cool mint-teal light Snowy Biomes: icy blue rays Desert, Savanna and Badlands: amber, orange and terracotta light Oceans: aqua, turquoise and deep blue Mushroom Fields: violet-magenta haze Pink sunsets and sunrises. At dusk and dawn the sky blends from dusky violet at the top to rose-pink around the sun. The sunlight itself turns pink, so the rays at that time of day glow pink too. This is the best moment to look for light shafts. Moody rain. During rain the haze turns a cool blue-grey, only lightly tinted by the biome, so storms feel wet and atmospheric. Deep, glowing nights. Night skies are a rich navy-indigo with soft blue moonlight. Lanterns, torches and glow berries stand out warmly against the dark. A dramatic End. The End has a magenta-purple haze with a golden-orange beam of light cutting through it, plus its own colour grading. A redesigned Nether. Nether wastes, Crimson Forest, Warped Forest, Soul Sand Valley and Basalt Deltas each have their own sky, light colour and ambient glow. Matching water and colour. Water surfaces are tuned to each biome. A gentle colour-grading pass adds a little contrast and saturation without crushing shadows or blowing out highlights. Two Versions CLASSIC VISUALS: the main pack, with rich, clearly visible colour. CLASSIC VISUALS (Soft): the same idea with gentler rays, for a more natural look. How to Use It Import the .mcpack file by tapping or double-clicking it. Go to Settings, then Global Resources, and activate CLASSIC VISUALS. Turn on Vibrant Visuals in Video Settings. For the best rays, explore at sunrise or sunset, near trees, hills or clouds where light is broken up. Tips Use only one Vibrant Visuals pack at a time to avoid conflicts. If the effect feels too strong, switch to the Soft version. Light shafts are strongest when the sun is low and something casts shadows. fullDescription: Original work by : PngBR JUST A DREAM . Alpha Dreams is a nostalgic Minecraft Bedrock resource pack inspired by the early days of Minecraft, Alpha, Beta and the classic Pocket Edition era. The project began as Old Craft, but evolved far beyond its original concept. Alpha Dreams aims to recreate the atmosphere, colors, textures and visual identity of old Minecraft while keeping the pack playable on modern Bedrock versions. ✦ What is Alpha Dreams? Alpha Dreams is more than just an old-style texture pack. The goal is to make modern Minecraft feel like a forgotten version of the game, combining classic textures, old Pocket Edition aesthetics, retro interfaces, nostalgic sounds and other details inspired by Minecraft's early history. The pack currently includes two different visual experiences: Alpha Textures A visual style inspired by Minecraft's early Alpha era. This subpack focuses on the simpler, rougher and more experimental appearance of early Minecraft, with classic-looking textures, old colors and a more primitive atmosphere. Beta Textures A separate visual style inspired by Minecraft Beta and the classic Pocket Edition era. Beta Textures features its own block textures, color maps, menu panoramas and other visual differences, creating a more colorful and recognizable old-school Pocket Edition feeling. Switching between Alpha and Beta changes more than a few textures. Each subpack is designed to represent a different period of Minecraft's visual history. ✦ Features • Alpha-inspired textures • Beta/Pocket Edition-inspired textures • Alpha and Beta subpacks • Old-style touchscreen controls • Retro HUD elements • Classic-looking hotbar and interface elements • Old-style menu presentation • Animated title fade-in • Animated splash text • Custom Alpha Dreams logo • Custom Minecraft-style panoramas • Alternate Beta panoramas • Legacy-inspired block textures • Legacy-inspired item textures • Classic End-related textures • Old-style End Portal Frame • Custom moon phases • Updated painting textures • Custom pumpkin overlay • Hundreds of splash texts • Retro-inspired food and item textures • Custom grass and foliage color maps • Different visual variations between Alpha and Beta • Support for modern Bedrock versions ✦ A Different Kind of Nostalgia Alpha Dreams does not try to recreate one specific Minecraft version perfectly. Instead, it explores the feeling of remembering Minecraft from years ago. Alpha represents the early, experimental days. Beta represents the colorful era that many players experienced through early Minecraft and Pocket Edition. The result is a mixture of old textures, modern Minecraft and memories from different periods of the game's history. ✦ Development Alpha Dreams is an evolving project. The current 1.0.4 release marks the transition from Days At The Origins into the Alpha Dreams era and introduces the Alpha and Beta subpack system, expanded legacy textures, retro controls, new UI elements, custom panoramas and many other changes. More content is planned for future updates, including additional legacy models, sounds, interface elements and a Modern subpack designed to reinterpret newer Minecraft content through the Alpha Dreams aesthetic. ✦ Credits Created by PngBR. Alpha Dreams is a fan-made Minecraft Bedrock resource pack created for nostalgic purposes. Minecraft is owned by Mojang Studios and Microsoft.

fullDescription: Borderful Glowing Ores Caves are dark, and finding ore usually means burning through a stack of torches just to see what you're swinging at. This pack fixes that. With Vibrant Visuals on, every ore glows with its own emissive light. Diamond shines pale blue from across a ravine, redstone burns red in the dark, and gold catches your eye the moment you round a corner. No behaviour pack, no commands, no lag. ⛏ Two Styles, One Pack Default Glowing Ores The subtle option. Only the ore itself glows, exactly where the mineral sits in the stone. Nothing is outlined, so it just looks like the ore is lit. Best if you want realism and don't want your world to look modded. Borderful Glowing Ores The visibility option. Every ore block gets a coloured, glowing border on top of the glowing ore, so it reads instantly at a distance and in dim light. Great for resource gathering, speedrunning, or anyone who mines with brightness turned down. Swap between the two styles any time in the pack settings, no reinstall needed. 🧩 Compatibility It's 100% resource pack, with no behaviour pack, so achievements stay enabled and it's safe to add to an existing world. It works alongside shaders, PVP packs and other resource packs. Just keep Borderful Glowing Ores above them so its ore textures win. ✅ Compatible with Actions & Stuff Tested with Actions & Stuff by Oreville Studios, and both packs work together. Put Borderful Glowing Ores above Actions & Stuff in your active pack list and the glow works as normal. 🌟 What's Covered Every ore in the game Coal, copper, iron, gold, diamond, emerald, lapis and redstone, plus all their deepslate versions, nether gold ore, nether quartz ore and ancient debris. Beyond ore Amethyst clusters and all three bud stages, the amethyst on calibrated sculk sensors, and cauldron water all get emissive maps too, so geodes light up the same way your mineshaft does. Coloured block light The pack also sets custom light colours for over 100 light-emitting blocks in Vibrant Visuals: torches, soul torches, lanterns, copper torches and lanterns, campfires, candles in every colour, froglights, glowstone, sea lanterns, lava, lit redstone ore and more. Real PBR texture sets These are proper PBR texture sets with tuned emissive and height maps, not brightened colour textures. The glow works with Minecraft's lighting instead of looking like a flat sticker pasted on the wall. Turn The Glow On This is the one step people miss. The glow comes from Minecraft's PBR pipeline, so it only shows up when Vibrant Visuals is active: ➤ Settings → Video → Graphics Mode → Vibrant Visuals (or Ray Tracing, on supported devices) ➤ Move Borderful Glowing Ores to the top of your active resource pack list ➤ Requires Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.80 or newer If your ores look completely normal, it's almost always because Vibrant Visuals is still off. Flip that switch and they'll light up immediately. 🚀 Performance The pack adds no entities and no scripts. It only swaps texture and lighting data, so on its own it costs essentially zero FPS. Vibrant Visuals is the demanding part, and that's Minecraft's renderer, not this pack. If your device runs Vibrant Visuals, it runs Borderful Glowing Ores. 💖 Support Over half a million downloads, thank you! If this pack made your caves better, a rating or a comment really helps, and it's what keeps the updates coming. Found a bug or want an ore handled differently? Leave a comment and I'll take a look. Light up your caves, spot the good stuff from across the room, and stop wasting torches. Happy mining!

fullDescription: Clear & Borderless Glass for Minecraft Bedrock 1.26 — three tiny packs that fix ugly glass Glass is one of the best building blocks in Minecraft — right up until you actually look through it. In vanilla Bedrock every glass block carries a thick, opaque frame, so a wall of glass ends up looking like a spreadsheet instead of a window. Clear & Borderless Glass is a set of three standalone resource packs that remove that frame, keep the transparency, and let your builds finally look the way you imagined them. No subpacks, no settings, no behaviour pack, no experimental toggles. You pick one file, you tap it, and your glass changes. The problem with vanilla glass Open any modern house build and look through the windows. What you see is not the view — it is a grid of white borders stacked on top of the view. Two things make it worse: The frame is per block, not per pane. A 6×4 window is 24 blocks, so you get 24 frames instead of one window frame. The frame is fully opaque , so it survives any lighting, any shader and any angle. That is fine when glass is decoration. It is painful when the glass is the point of the build: aquariums, greenhouses, sky bridges, ocean monuments, modern villas, observation decks, mob farms with glass walls. The three variants Pack File Look Best for Borderless Glass release/borderless-glass.mcpack The frame is gone; only four small corner dots remain Big window walls, aquariums, greenhouses Clear Glass release/clear-glass.mcpack Fully transparent centre with a thin, visible frame Builds where glass must still read as glass Clear & Borderless Glass release/clear-borderless-glass.mcpack Transparent centre and no frame at all The cleanest look — glass that disappears All three cover the same 35 textures, so nothing is missing when you switch: plain glass tinted_glass all 16 stained glass colours the matching 16 glass_pane_top textures (the pane face) Because the packs are three separate files with three different UUIDs, you can install all of them at the same time and activate a different one per world without any conflict. How to install Download the .mcpack you want. Open the file — Minecraft Bedrock launches and imports the pack automatically. Open your world → Settings → Resource Packs → activate the pack. Done. There is no subpack menu and nothing else to configure. It is a pure resource pack: it never touches your world data, so it is safe to add to and remove from an existing survival world, and it works on Realms and servers (client side). Performance Textures are the original 16×16 resolution, so the packs weigh ~90 KB each and cost nothing in FPS — they are the same size files the game already loads, just redrawn. Requirements Minecraft Bedrock 1.26.0 or newer ( min_engine_version: [1, 26, 0] ). No experimental toggles, no Beta APIs, no behaviour pack. Works on Windows, Android, iOS, Xbox, PlayStation and Switch. Asset Path Master video (1:41, 1920×1080) video/clear-borderless-glass-full-video.mp4 Shorts (30s / 29s / 43s, 1080×1920) video/shorts/*.mp4 Thumbnails media/thumbnails/ Pack icons (256×256) source/icons/ Subtitles (AR + EN) video/subtitles-*.srt , video/shorts/*-ar.srt , *-en.srt Frequently asked questions Do I need all three? No. Install the one you like; install all three if you want to switch per world. Can I use it with other resource packs? Yes — put this pack above packs that also touch glass, or below packs that should win. Is it allowed on Realms / servers? Yes. It is client-side only; nobody else has to install it to see their own glass, and it changes no gameplay. (C) Youseef-Tools & IgnisMod

title: Invisible Item Frames No more invisible mobs
description: Invisible Item Frames is a lightweight Minecraft Bedrock resource pack that makes both regular and glow item frames completely invisible while keeping all vanilla functionality intact.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: # Invisible Item Frames Create cleaner displays by hiding the frame and letting the item become part of your build. **Invisible Item Frames** is a Minecraft Bedrock Resource Pack that removes the visible model of Item Frames while keeping the items placed inside them visible and fully usable. Display maps, tools, weapons, blocks, signs, decorations, and other items directly against walls and surfaces without the normal wooden frame surrounding them. With selectable subpacks, you can now decide whether you want to hide **both frame types, only regular Item Frames, or only Glow Item Frames**. ## Choose Which Item Frames Are Invisible Not every build needs both types of Item Frames hidden, so Invisible Item Frames includes multiple subpack options. Choose from: * **Both Item Frames (Default)** – Regular Item Frames and Glow Item Frames are invisible. * **Item Frame Only** – Only regular Item Frames are invisible. Glow Item Frames retain their normal appearance. * **Glow Item Frame Only** – Only Glow Item Frames are invisible. Regular Item Frames retain their normal appearance. The **Both Item Frames** option is selected by default, giving you the traditional Invisible Item Frames experience immediately after enabling the pack. You can change the subpack whenever you want from the Resource Pack settings. ## What Does the Pack Change? Invisible Item Frames changes the visual appearance of the selected Item Frame types without changing how they function. When a frame is hidden, the item placed inside it remains visible. You can still: * Place Item Frames normally * Add items to them * Rotate displayed items * Remove displayed items * Break the frame * Use regular and Glow Item Frames * Build with them exactly as you normally would There are no custom items, commands, menus, or complicated setup procedures. Place a frame, add an item, and start decorating. ## Build Cleaner Displays Removing the visible frame allows displayed items to blend directly into your builds instead of looking like objects mounted inside a wooden border. Invisible Item Frames are especially useful for: * Map walls * Storage labels * Tool and weapon displays * Shop displays * Decorative furniture * Kitchens and workshops * Hidden organization systems * Interior decoration * Signs and visual markers * Custom wall decorations * Detailed Survival bases For example, you can place an item against a wall as decoration and make it appear as though the item itself is attached directly to the surface. Storage rooms can use blocks or items as visual labels without covering the walls with visible Item Frames. ## Regular and Glow Item Frame Support Both major Item Frame types are supported. **Regular Item Frames** can be hidden while continuing to hold and display items normally. **Glow Item Frames** can also be hidden while retaining their brighter displayed-item appearance. Because each type can now be controlled through subpacks, you aren't required to make both invisible. Want invisible regular frames but normal Glow Item Frames? You can do that. Want only your Glow Item Frames hidden? That's an option too. Or simply leave the pack on the default setting to make both invisible. ## Designed to Avoid Unrelated Rendering Problems Invisible Item Frames uses a targeted Resource Pack approach designed specifically around the resources needed for Item Frames. Some methods of making Item Frames invisible can interfere with shared Minecraft rendering resources, potentially causing unexpected visual problems with unrelated entities. This pack is designed to keep its changes focused on Item Frames rather than unnecessarily modifying resources used throughout the game. The goal is simple: **hide the selected Item Frames without making unrelated mobs or entities disappear.** ## Proper Particle Support Invisible Item Frames also includes the required texture registration for Item Frame particles. This prevents the black-and-pink missing-texture particles that can occur when an invisible frame references a texture Minecraft cannot find. The pack includes: * Proper Item Frame break particles * Valid terrain texture registration * Correct terrain-atlas references * No intentional missing-texture particle effects The frames stay invisible while their interactions continue to look clean. ## Resource Pack Only Invisible Item Frames is entirely a **Resource Pack**. It does not require: * A Behavior Pack * Minecraft scripting * Script APIs * Experimental Beta APIs * Commands * Custom gameplay systems There is no administration menu or world configuration process to manage. Activate the Resource Pack, select your preferred subpack, and use Item Frames normally. ## Vibrant Visuals Compatible Invisible Item Frames is configured with support for Minecraft Bedrock's modern rendering features, including **Vibrant Visuals**. The pack is intended to provide its invisible-frame effect without requiring Vibrant Visuals to be disabled. Your exact visual experience can still depend on your device, Minecraft version, graphics settings, and other Resource Packs being used at the same time. ## Achievement Friendly Because Invisible Item Frames is a visual Resource Pack and does not require cheats, commands, scripts, or a Behavior Pack, it is designed for normal Survival worlds where achievements are enabled. It does not change game rules or provide command-based gameplay advantages. Minecraft ultimately determines achievement eligibility based on your world's settings and any other packs or features enabled in that world. ## Compatibility Invisible Item Frames is designed for **Minecraft Bedrock Edition** and can be used in: * Survival worlds * Creative worlds * Single-player worlds * Multiplayer worlds * Minecraft Realms * Bedrock servers It can also be used alongside other addons and Resource Packs as long as they do not replace the same Item Frame resources. If another Resource Pack modifies Item Frames, Minecraft's Resource Pack priority can determine which pack's changes are displayed. ## Installation 1. Download Invisible Item Frames. 2. Open the pack to import it into Minecraft Bedrock Edition. 3. Open the settings for the world where you want to use it. 4. Activate **Invisible Item Frames** under Resource Packs. 5. Select your preferred subpack: * Both Item Frames * Item Frame Only * Glow Item Frame Only 6. Enter the world. 7. Place an Item Frame and add an item. That's it. ## Simple by Design Invisible Item Frames doesn't turn Item Frames into a complicated new gameplay system. It does one thing and gives you control over how it does it: **Hide the frame so the displayed item can become part of your build.** Hide both frame types, hide only regular Item Frames, or hide only Glow Item Frames. Choose the style that fits your build and start decorating.

fullDescription: # Gojo UI A custom interface pack for **Minecraft Bedrock Edition** and **MCPE**. Gojo UI gives Minecraft a cleaner menu layout, extra HUD information, and a custom title-screen background. It is a **resource pack only**. It does not add new items, mobs, or worlds. --- ## What you get ### Custom menus - Redesigned start screen with a side menu - Cleaner play, pause, settings, and chat screens - Worlds and friends combined on one play screen - Custom buttons, icons, dialogs, and fonts - Import world / export world / quick play buttons shown on mobile - World folder name shown in the world list (Windows, iOS, Android) ### HUD extras - Compass, clock, and recovery compass on the HUD - XP amount and XP percent - Boss bar percent - Held-item durability - Arrow count while holding a bow or crossbow - Chunk position (on by default) - Optional Overworld / Nether coordinates - Optional item ID label - Inventory overlay on the HUD (Tab on PC; toggle on mobile) - Chat docked lower, closer to Java-style chat - F1-style hide GUI button for touch ### Inventory helpers Best in **Classic UI**: - Quick-craft button - Auto-move / auto-drop / creative destroy modes - Chest take-all / dump buttons - Empty-slot and held-item counters ### World look - Grass sides use the top grass texture - Clearer water and much less underwater / lava fog - Block-break, explosion, and splash-potion particles turned down - Pumpkin and spyglass overlays made easier to see through --- ## Theme The menu wallpaper is a custom Gojo-inspired background. Menus stay on the left. The artwork fills the rest of the screen. --- ## Install 1. Download **Gojo UI.mcpack**. 2. Open the file so Minecraft imports it. 3. Go to **Settings → Global Resources** and turn **Gojo UI** on. You can also enable it on a single world. 5. Restart your Minecraft **Important:** restart the game after enabling the pack or some screens will not update. ### Load order - Use this pack as your main UI pack. - Put any extra background / theme packs **above** Gojo UI. --- ## Requirements - Minecraft Bedrock / MCPE - No behavior pack - Works in single player and on most servers (resource pack only) For the custom fonts to behave, English as the game language works best. --- ## Settings you can change Open the pack and edit `betmc_config/config.json` to toggle: - Chunk / dimension coordinates - Item ID label - Enchantment text on the HUD - World folder names on the play screen - Menu fonts (Noto Sans, Nunito, Comic Relief, Samsung One) - Custom background on or off Compass, clock, and similar HUD icons use numeric item IDs. After a big Minecraft update those IDs can change. If the wrong item appears on the HUD, update the IDs in that config file. --- ## Notes / known limits - This pack is based on a beta UI framework. A Minecraft update can shift menus. - Some inventory extras work only in **Classic UI**, not Pocket UI. - The HUD inventory overlay is more complete on PC than on mobile. - A music-player tab exists in settings, but music files are not included. --- ## Credits **Gojo UI** uses the **BetMC UI** framework by **BetSoi2411 / BetMC2411**. BetMC UI is licensed under **GNU GPL-3.0**. This pack keeps that license. Additional HUD / dialog / chat code credited in the original pack: - Asaki Yuki - TLGM2308 Background art is fan-made menu artwork for this pack. Satoru Gojo and Jujutsu Kaisen belong to their original owners. This is an unofficial fan project and is not approved by those owners or by Mojang / Microsoft. --- ## Support After installing, restart the game. If menus look mixed with another UI pack, disable the other UI pack or change the resource pack order.

title: Somber Shaders BE
description: An unofficial Bedrock recreation inspired by Somber Shaders. Horror minecraft bedrock resource pack that aims to recreate the nostalgic atmosphere of early beta/alpha versions with an eerie twist, inspired by ARGs.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: Somber — Bedrock Port A best effort Minecraft: Bedrock Edition port of Somber by Snorfield . A Bedrock Edition port of Somber , the Java shader that brings back the atmosphere of alpha and beta Minecraft with a few extra stuff. The pack is built for Vibrant Visuals & Raytracing , but it also works in the regular Fancy mode, with fewer features. Features Fog - The world fades into fog about 30 blocks out! Leaving distant trees and hills as faint silhouettes. The fog takes on the colour of the sky: soft blue by day, deep navy at dusk, near-black at night. Rain turns it a cold grey. Fog also thickens dynamically ! The fog covers the whole sky, so the horizon disappears. The sun and moon show only as faint glows. You can turn this off to get the open sky back. Water - Water is solid blue; you cannot see below the surface of the water. Every biome has its own water tint. Foliage - Grass & leaves get a punchy, saturated green from the beta version of mc. VFX (Screen Effects) - There are 3: vignette (the screen edges fade into darkness), film grain (flickering noise, sorta like an old camcorder), & chromatic aberration (a coloured lens fringe around the edges of your vision)! Shadows - Shade is a bit deeper, nights are completely dark, and caves are pitch black until you light a torch. Torches also emit a coloured light, not just one fixed color. Sunlight casts blocky, pixelated shadows. Sun & Moon Brightness - The sun and moon are brighter, as in the original shader. You'll see this best with the sky overlay turned off Requirements This pack is best with Vibrant Visuals , though Fancy graphics also suffices! Requires Minecraft: Bedrock v1.26.0 or newer. Vibrant Visuals' Hardware Requirements: Windows : Graphics cards and drivers supporting DirectX 12 Intel GPUs: Intel graphics driver version 31.0.101.3430 or later is required Android: Android devices running on Adreno 640 (something likke Snapdragon 855), Mali-G68 / Mali-G77 (Valhall architecture, like MediaTek 1000 series), Maleoon , PowerVR A-Series , or Xclipse 530 or higher IOS/iPadOS: An iPhone or iPad running on an A12 Bionic , M1 chip , or higher (like teh iPhone XR, iPhone SE 2nd gen, and newer) Customising Somber Slider option What it does Screen Effects: Off Removes the vignette, grain & lens fringe for a clean image Vignette: Off Removes the dark screen edges Chromatic Aberration: Off Removes the coloured lens fringe Noise: Off Removes the film grain Old Foliage Vibrance: Off Puts grass and leaves back to normal Minecraft colours Water Transparency: On Makes water see-through again Fog Sky Overlay: Off Clears the sky so you can see the sun, moon and stars Fog: Off Removes the Somber fog completely Fog Strength: Light Thinner fog that lets you see a lot further Fog Strength: Heavy Thicker, more clautrophobic fog Preset: Subtle A gentler version of everything Preset: Intense Stronger vingette, grain, fog and greener foliage Preset: Nightmare Everything at maximum, with fog closing in within about 10 blocks 👻 Somber (Default) The original Somber look Dependencies This pack looks amazing if paired with the Classic Textures resource pack for Minecraft: Bedrock. Just make sure Somber is at the very bottom of your enabled packs in your world pack settings/global resource settings; otherwise, it won't look very good. Here is the link to the dependency. fullDescription: oSkullo's CPS Counter Keep track of your attack speed and combat performance in real-time. This resource pack adds a clean, customizable CPS counter directly to your HUD, powered entirely by the modern Bedrock UI settings array. You can adjust exactly how the counter looks and where it sits on your screen without ever leaving the game. The Honest Truth: How It Works Due to the technical limitations of the Minecraft Bedrock UI engine, it is impossible to read raw hardware inputs (mouse clicks or screen taps) directly. Because of this, this pack functions as a Hand-Swing Counter. It detects the left-click attacks landed in the last real second based on your character's arm animation. What this means: It is highly accurate for normal gameplay, PvP, and standard clicking. However, if you are drag-clicking or using macros at extreme speeds (20+ CPS), the counter will not maintain a 1:1 ratio with your hardware because the in-game swing animation simply cannot keep up with those speeds. Features & In-Game Customization Taking advantage of the settings array for Minecraft 1.21.0+, you have full control over the HUD element directly from the pack settings: Visibility Controls: Toggle the entire counter on or off, or choose to hide the "CPS" text label to just show the raw numbers. Positioning: Freely move the counter anywhere on your screen using the X (Left/Right) and Y (Up/Down) offset sliders. Scaling: Adjust the size of the counter from a subtle 25% up to a massive 300%. Background Settings: Toggle the dark background on or off, and fine-tune its opacity (0% to 100%) to ensure it never blocks your crosshair visibility. Compatibility Fully compatible with mobile, PC, and console. Created by oSkullo YouTube: oSkullo Discord: discord.gg/oSkullo

title: GURJAR X Noir Shader
description: GURJAR X Noir Shader transforms Minecraft Bedrock into a dramatic black-and-white world — deep contrast, moody shadows and cinematic monochrome lighting inspired by classic film noir.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: GURJAR X Noir Shader is a lightweight, single-style visual pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, built on Mojang's native Vibrant Visuals render pipeline. Where every other filter in this series leans into color — Vivid's saturation, Cartoon's punch, Retro's warmth — Noir strips it all away and goes in the opposite direction entirely: a bold, dramatic, almost entirely monochrome world built around light, shadow, and contrast rather than hue. Color Grading — This is the heart of the Noir identity. Saturation is pushed down to nearly zero across shadows, midtones, and highlights alike, stripping color out of the entire scene and leaving behind a true black-and-white presentation. But this isn't a flat grayscale filter slapped over the top — contrast and gamma are carefully tuned so that blacks stay deep and rich, whites stay bright and clean, and the full tonal range in between remains readable and detailed, exactly like classic film noir cinematography. The result feels less like a color image with the saturation turned down and more like the game was shot on black-and-white film from the start. Lighting — Noir leans hard into dramatic, high-contrast lighting. Rather than smooth, even illumination, the sun's brightness and positioning are tuned to create striking pools of light against darker surroundings — long shadows, bright highlights, and a strong sense of directionality. This is what gives Noir its "dramatic lighting" character: scenes feel staged and cinematic, with light doing as much storytelling as the landscape itself. Atmospherics — Sky scattering is tuned to support the monochrome mood — soft, moody, and atmospheric rather than colorful, so skies read as bright fog-like gradients of light and dark instead of blue expanses. This keeps the focus on shape, silhouette, and contrast, the classic visual language of noir film. Shadows — Noir uses more defined, higher-contrast shadow rendering than the softer filters in this series, reinforcing the dramatic, high-contrast aesthetic. Shadows aren't just present — they're part of the composition, adding depth and mood to builds, caves, and forests alike. Water — Even without color, water keeps its natural wave motion and caustic detailing, appearing as shimmering light and dark patterns rather than colored ripples, fitting naturally into the monochrome world without looking flat or lifeless. Because this pack uses a proper dedicated subpack structure (rather than a root-only setup), it loads reliably and automatically the moment it's enabled — no slider, no filter menu, no risk of silent failure. Enable it, and the Noir look is active immediately, every time you load into a world. Noir works especially well for atmospheric builds, horror maps, detective/mystery-themed servers, black-and-white photography-style screenshots, or simply for players who want to experience familiar terrain in a completely new, moody light. Requirements: Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.80+, with the Vibrant Visuals experimental toggle enabled at world creation, on a device capable of running the deferred rendering pipeline. Install: Tap the .mcpack file to import it into Minecraft, then activate only this pack under Resource Packs before creating or loading a world. If you've previously installed Cinematic, Vivid, Retro, Cartoon, or Standard from this series, make sure they are disabled or removed first — only one shader-style pack should be active at a time. 🙌 Credits - GURJAR

Shadows — Soft-filtered shadows with natural falloff keep the world grounded and three-dimensional without harsh, distracting edges, matching the overall calm, dependable character of this style. fullDescription: Golden Horizon Visuals is a cinematic Minecraft Bedrock Vibrant Visuals resource pack created by Baku_Studio, designed to transform ordinary Minecraft scenes into warm, atmospheric, and visually rich environments inspired by cinematic golden-hour landscapes. The visual identity of Golden Horizon Visuals is built around carefully balanced lighting, color grading, atmospheric depth, water enhancement, foliage tones, shadows, and sky coloration. Instead of completely replacing Minecraft’s recognizable visual style, the pack aims to enhance the existing Bedrock world while giving it a more polished and cinematic appearance. One of the main highlights of the pack is its warm natural lighting. Sunlight is designed to create a rich golden tone, particularly during sunrise and sunset, giving terrain, trees, structures, and vegetation a warm cinematic glow. Low-angle sunlight is intended to create stronger depth and more noticeable illumination across the environment while keeping the overall scene readable and visually balanced. The sky and atmosphere are another important part of the experience. Golden Horizon Visuals is designed with atmospheric depth in mind, helping distant mountains, forests, and terrain gradually blend into soft environmental haze instead of appearing completely flat. This creates stronger separation between foreground and background and gives large Minecraft landscapes a more expansive appearance. The pack also focuses heavily on water visuals. Water is intended to appear clearer and more visually noticeable, with enhanced color, lighting interaction, reflections, surface movement, and caustic-style illumination where supported by the Minecraft Bedrock Vibrant Visuals system. Different environments can benefit from different visual treatments so that water does not appear identical in every biome. Foliage and terrain colors are carefully balanced to keep Minecraft’s familiar identity intact. Grass remains naturally green, leaves retain their environmental character, wood keeps its warm appearance, and stone and other terrain materials maintain believable tones while receiving improved lighting and shadow interaction. Another major part of the experience is color grading. The pack uses stronger cinematic contrast, richer but controlled saturation, warm highlights, deeper shadows, and smoother transitions between bright and dark areas. The goal is to make Minecraft screenshots and gameplay look more dramatic without turning the world into an overly saturated or unrealistic scene. Golden Horizon Visuals is intended for players who enjoy cinematic Minecraft worlds, landscape exploration, screenshots, videos, building showcases, survival gameplay, and atmospheric environments. It can also be useful for creators who want their Bedrock worlds to have a more distinctive visual identity without changing their actual builds. The pack is designed around Minecraft Bedrock’s Vibrant Visuals rendering system and follows the appropriate resource-pack structure for the supported implementation. Compatibility should always be checked against the specific Minecraft Bedrock version being used, since Vibrant Visuals features and schemas can vary between game versions. title: Visuals Deferred
description: Visuals Deferred adds vivid colors, golden volumetric sun rays, glowing lights and dramatic sunrises to Minecraft Bedrock's Vibrant Visuals / Deferred Lighting.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: Visuals Deferred is a lighting-focused resource pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, designed to push Deferred Lighting (Vibrant Visuals) toward a warmer, brighter and far more colorful look. Every forest, river, sunrise and cherry grove has been tuned so that light becomes the star of the scene, without touching your gameplay. Whether you are exploring a misty forest at dawn, sailing along a quiet river, or building under a rain-soaked night sky, the pack keeps the image warm, readable and full of depth. GOLDEN SUN RAYS The biggest change is the volumetric fog. Air scattering has been increased in the forest, jungle, plains, cherry grove, taiga, swamp, desert and pale garden biomes, so sunlight cuts through the trees as soft, visible beams. Forests glow with golden-green shafts, jungles carry a fresh green haze, and cherry groves are wrapped in gentle pink light. The fog stays thin enough to keep the world clear, so you get atmosphere instead of a wall of haze. DRAMATIC SUNRISE AND SUNSET The sky has been rebuilt around richer colors. The sun is brighter, its halo is stronger, and the horizon now blends from deep orange into rose and violet before night falls. Dawn and dusk gain extra color stops, which makes every morning and evening feel cinematic. Midday skies are a cleaner, more saturated blue. VIVID, SATURATED COLORS Color grading has been raised across highlights, midtones and shadows, with a slightly warmer highlight tint and a small exposure lift. Grass, leaves, birch, spruce, swamp and mangrove color maps are more vibrant, and cherry leaves are a deeper, livelier pink. Shadows keep a soft blue-violet tone, so the scene never looks flat. GLOWING LIGHT SOURCES Emissive intensity has been increased, so lava, glowstone and other glowing blocks stand out clearly. Point light colors for torches, lanterns, campfires, candles, portals and more are brighter and more saturated, giving your builds and caves a warm, colorful glow. BIOME HIGHLIGHTS Forests and jungles are the stars, with strong beams filtering through the canopy. Plains and rivers get a bright, airy haze and glowing water. Cherry groves feel soft and dreamlike, with pink tones in both the air and the leaves. Taiga and cold biomes keep a cooler blue tint so they still feel like winter, while deserts pick up a warm, dusty gold. CLEARER, SPARKLING WATER Water uses cleaner teal-blue tones with slightly stronger wave detail. Biome water colors have been made richer, and underwater fog has been tuned for a brighter, more inviting look in rivers, lakes and oceans. MOODY NIGHTS Nights stay dark and atmospheric, but moonlight is a little bluer and stronger, so rain, shadows and moon shafts read clearly without losing the mood. REQUIREMENTS AND TIPS This pack needs Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.60 or newer and a device that supports Vibrant Visuals or Deferred Lighting. To install, open the .mcpack file with Minecraft, wait for the import message, then activate it in Global Resources and turn on Vibrant Visuals (or the Deferred Technical Preview on older versions). Keep it above other packs for the best result. If the image feels too bright on your screen, lower the exposure in the color grading file, or reduce the fog scattering values for less haze. Performance depends on your device, so lower the render distance if you notice slowdowns. Visuals Deferred is a tuned edition based on Visuality Deferred v2.1, and full credit goes to the original creators. Screenshots and feedback are always welcome, and if you share the pack, please keep the credits below intact. Enjoy the light! description: A cozy autumn-toned Vibrant Visuals shader fused with a full 256x pixel-outline texture set. Every block, item and mob gets a crisp, hand-inked bevel outline under a warm golden pumpkin-spice sky — richer PBR lighting, deeper colors, sharp ..
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: Spice Outline Texture Pack takes two ideas that were never meant to be separate and finally puts them in one pack: a warm, cinematic autumn shader, and a texture set where every single pixel is outlined. At its core is an enhanced Vibrant Visuals (PBR) shader built on a fall-themed lighting profile. The sun carries a deep amber-to-rose color curve as it moves across the sky, shifting from a soft golden white at midday to a rich orange-red glow near the horizon. A cool blue ambient fill light sits underneath it, so warm highlights and cool shadows play off each other instead of everything looking flat and orange. The sky itself uses a hand-tuned gradient — blue zenith fading into pink, coral and amber near the horizon — with boosted atmospheric scattering so sunsets feel genuinely dramatic rather than a simple color swap. On top of the original shader, this build pushes it further: midtone and shadow saturation is raised for punchier color, ACES filmic tone-mapping is kept for cinematic contrast, shadow maps are doubled in resolution (1024 → 2048) for crisper detail under trees and structures, water carries slightly more visible wave detail and clarity, and distant fog was shifted from a neutral gray-blue into a warm golden haze — so far-off hills disappear into an autumn glow instead of a cold mist. Then comes the outline layer. Every block, tool, weapon, mob, cloud, and even the sun and moon are rendered with a thin bevel: a warm cream highlight on the top and right edge of every texture pixel, and a deep umber shadow on the bottom and left. Blown up at 256x resolution, the result is a mosaic, stained-glass-like look — each block face reads as a grid of individually outlined tiles instead of a flat smear of color. Blocks that the shader recolors for the fall theme (leaves, ores, swords, lava, and more) were run back through the same outline process by hand, so the whole world — shader-recolored blocks and vanilla blocks alike — carries one consistent, unified art style instead of two textures fighting each other. PBR support carries through as well: normal maps and metalness/emissive/roughness maps were resized and pixel-aligned to match the new texture resolution, so surface lighting, specular highlights, and emissive glow (torches, lanterns, lava, glowstone, and more) still read correctly under the new shader. Requirements: Minecraft Bedrock 1.26 or newer, with PBR / Vibrant Visuals graphics enabled in Video settings (requires a compatible GPU or the software PBR fallback). Note on style: true screen-space cel-shading (a solid white outline traced around whole objects, like in the concept image) isn't something Bedrock resource packs can do — that's a Java Edition shader-loader technique (Iris/OptiFine). What this pack does is the closest thing achievable within Bedrock's actual capabilities: the outline is baked directly into every texture at the pixel level, which reads as a strong, consistent outline effect in-world, especially at this resolution. fullDescription: GURJAR X Cinematic Shader is a lightweight, single-style visual pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, built on Mojang's native Vibrant Visuals render pipeline. Instead of overwhelming you with multiple filters to choose from, this pack focuses on doing one thing exceptionally well: delivering a warm, dramatic, movie-like atmosphere that makes every sunrise, sunset, and quiet lakeside moment feel cinematic. Lighting & Sky — The sun and moon follow custom illuminance and color curves that shift through deep ambers, soft pinks, and cool blues across the day/night cycle, so golden hour genuinely feels golden. Mie scattering and horizon blending are fine-tuned for a hazy, atmospheric sky instead of the flat vanilla look. Color Grading — A Hable tone-mapping curve, combined with separate midtone, highlight, and shadow grading, gives the image richer contrast, warmer highlights, and slightly cool, desaturated shadows — the same technique real films use to visually separate light from dark. Shadows — Soft shadow filtering with a wider texel size produces gentler, more natural shadow edges instead of harsh vanilla pixelation. Water — Custom wave shape, wind-driven ripples, and a dedicated caustics texture add depth and motion to oceans, rivers, and lakes, making water feel alive rather than a flat blue texture. No sliders, no subpack menu — enable the pack and the cinematic look is active by default. Requirements: Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.80+, with the Vibrant Visuals experimental toggle enabled in world settings, on a device capable of running the deferred rendering pipeline. Without Vibrant Visuals enabled, these effects won't appear.
